epic.intent:
Make the desktop app look like it belongs to the Adeptus Mechanicus, matching the app icon.

**Today:** the renderer uses a generic graphite "forge console" palette with an amber accent (`src/renderer/src/styles.css`), and the sidebar brand is a stroke hex glyph. The chibi tech-priest appears in the dock/taskbar and the favicon, but nowhere a person actually looks inside the app.

**Outcome:** a palette taken from the icon (Mars crimson hood and robe, bone/ivory cog trim, brass fittings, gunmetal respirator, with the green cybernetic lens as a sparing highlight) applied across the shell, sidebar, home, epic workspace, plan graph, ticket panel and checkpoint screens. The tech-priest becomes the sidebar brand mark and greets people on the welcome and onboarding screens.

**Why:** the app should feel like one product with its icon, and the palette change is a chance to route every color through tokens and guard contrast with a test.

**Out of scope:** layout or information-architecture changes, new features, a light theme, new fonts, regenerating the icon artwork, and packaging icons (`build/icon.icns`, `build/icon.ico`; done in board epic 019).

**Bundled bug fix:** taking one epic out of draft currently takes every epic out of draft. It is fixed in sprint 1 so later sprints can run with several epics open.

successCriteria.text: The desktop app's colors come from a Mechanicus palette derived from the app icon (crimson, bone, brass, gunmetal), documented in `docs/design/palette.md`.
Every renderer color flows through `:root` tokens in `src/renderer/src/styles.css`; no component stylesheet hardcodes a hex color.
The sidebar brand shows the tech-priest icon with the tagline "All hail the machine spirit" under the name, and the welcome and onboarding screens show the mascot.
Every ticket and run state stays distinguishable from the brand colors and from each other, and always shows its text label.
Body text and state labels meet WCAG AA contrast (at least 4.5:1) on their surfaces, enforced by a unit test.
Lint, typecheck, unit tests, fireguard, deadcode and build pass on the integrated branch.
Saving, discarding or changing the status of one epic leaves every other epic's draft untouched, covered by a regression test.

The plan graph and the checkpoint and overview screens are readable: sprint labels never overlap checkpoint dividers, a completed epic's overview can always be reopened, and its text wraps at a normal reading width.

epic.title: Mechanicus UI revamp: crimson, brass and the tech-priest mascot

bundle.rationale:
**Shape.** Two sprints. Sprint 1 does the safe groundwork in parallel (token consolidation, the palette proposal, the sidebar brand mark), so the sprint 1 checkpoint is a real decision: the person approves the palette before anyone applies it. Sprint 2 applies the palette (with a contrast guard test written first), then restyles the shell and the epic workspace in parallel, adds the mascot to the first-run screens, and ends with an integration ticket.

**Critical path:** palette (or token consolidation) → apply palette → shell or workspace restyle → integrate.

**Integration ticket.** The shell restyle and the mascot ticket both edit `src/renderer/src/styles.css`, and the workspace restyle edits the shared tones, so the integration ticket owns merging, conflict resolution, the full check suite, the design README, and evidence for each success criterion.

**Assumptions** (from a one-line request; change any of these before saving):
- The app stays dark-only, with IBM Plex type and the current layout. This is a color and branding pass, not a redesign.
- Crimson is the primary accent, brass the secondary, bone for display text. The lens green appears sparingly.
- The icon artwork is final. Packaging icons are already done (board epic 019), so this epic only uses the icon inside the renderer.
- The static mockups in `docs/design/mockups/` are not regenerated. The README notes that they predate the revamp.
- Visual changes are verified with screenshots attached to submissions, and contrast is enforced by a unit test.

**Bug fix in sprint 1.** The "one epic out of draft takes every epic out of draft" bug runs in sprint 1, in parallel with the groundwork. It touches no theme files, and fixing it early keeps the person's other drafts safe while this epic is saved and re-saved. The integration ticket requires it so success criterion s7 is verified with the rest.

**Graph and overview bug fixes in sprint 1.** Three reported layout and persistence bugs are fixed in sprint 1: sprint text overlapping the checkpoint divider, the completed overview disappearing, and the overview's one-word-wide text. The text bug waits for the persistence fix, because the overview can't be reopened until then. The workspace restyle waits for both layout fixes, so it restyles correct layouts and doesn't collide in `graph.css` and `checkpoint.css`.

The sidebar brand shows the tech-priest icon and the "All hail the machine spirit" tagline, and the favicon matches the current icon.
Acting on one epic's draft no longer changes any other epic's draft, proven by a regression test.
Sprint labels no longer overlap checkpoint dividers, and a completed epic's overview can be reopened and reads at a normal width.

- `epic/tones.css`: `#e8b86a` (`.ew-tone-edited`)

tickets.body:
Decide the new color tokens before anyone touches the theme. Take the palette from the chibi tech-priest in `build/icon.png` (the master is `build/mechanicus-cute-master.png`): Mars crimson hood and robe, bone/ivory cog trim, brass fittings, gunmetal respirator, and the green cybernetic lens.

Write `docs/design/palette.md` with:

1. **Token table.** Every color token in `:root` of `src/renderer/src/styles.css` (surfaces, lines, text, accent, states, danger, and the tokens added by the token-consolidation ticket), each with its current value, proposed value and role.
2. **Roles.** The primary accent (primary buttons, focus ring, selection, active sidebar row), the secondary accent (rules, highlights, links), display/heading ink, and where the green lens glow is allowed. Use it sparingly, for example the brand glow or the running indicator.
3. **Collision rules.** The crimson accent must not read as `--st-failed` or `--danger`, and the lens green must not read as `--st-accepted`. Re-tune state colors where needed and say how each state stays distinct (hue distance plus its text label).
4. **Contrast table** (WCAG 2.x ratios) for `--ink`, `--ink-2` and `--muted` on `--bg`, `--panel`, `--panel-2` and `--sidebar`; every `--st-*` on `--panel`; `--accent-ink` on `--accent`; `--danger-ink` on `--danger`. Body text and state labels need at least 4.5:1. `--faint` (decorative only) needs at least 3:1.

Starting samples from the icon (approximate, so check them against the image): crimson about `#b3201c` to `#c62a22`, deep hood shadow about `#480101`, bone trim about `#deba94` to `#e9dcc0`, brass about `#b5893a`, gunmetal about `#2a2624`, lens green about `#84c20a`.

Keep the dark-only theme, the IBM Plex fonts and the current layout. **Out of scope:** editing any stylesheet. The "Apply the Mechanicus palette" ticket does that once the person approves this doc at the sprint 1 checkpoint.

reasoning.rationale: Balancing brand hues against distinct state colors and contrast takes deliberate trade-offs.

tickets.body:
**Reported 2026-10-01:** "when you pull one epic out of draft it pulls all epics out of draft." An action on one epic's draft changes the draft state of every other epic.

**Reproduce first.** The exact action is not pinned down yet. Set up two or more open epics that each have a draft, in one tracked folder and also across two folders. Then try each of these:
- save a draft (DraftBar **Save**, or `save_plan`);
- discard a draft;
- move an epic between Backlog and In progress, or start or queue a run;
- switch between the Draft and Saved views in the workspace.

After each action, check every *other* epic: its sidebar `draft` badge and "Draft · not saved" status line, `hasDraft` and `draftRevision` from `list_epics`, and its workspace view.

**Already ruled out, by reading the code (no tests yet):**
- The draft SQL in `src/core/services/drafts.ts` and `settleDraft` in `src/core/services/plans.ts` all filter by `epic_id`.
- `EpicWorkspace` remounts per folder and epic (it is keyed), so its reducer's `view` is not shared between epics.

**Still suspect:**
- renderer state shared across epics: `app/useEpicLists.ts`, `app/eventRouting.ts` and `app/useRefreshTick.ts` (refresh after a change), `sidebar/epicStatusLine.ts`;
- the desktop IPC handlers and workspace pool in `src/main/desktop/`;
- portable export and import (`src/core/repo/portable.ts`, `importer.ts`) rewriting other epics' files.

**A related oddity to explain or fix:** on this epic, right after revision 1 was saved, a new draft identical to the saved plan existed (`hasDraft: true`, `draftRevision: 1`). The sidebar would then show "Has unsaved draft changes" when nothing is unsaved.

**Fix TDD-first:** first write a failing regression test at the lowest layer where the bug lives (core service, IPC handler or renderer), then fix the bug. Also add an integration test in `src/integration/` with two epics, proving that an action on one leaves the other's draft untouched.

**Out of scope:** UI restyling. This ticket is independent of the palette work.

reasoning.rationale: The root cause is unknown and could be in the core services, the IPC layer or renderer state, so it needs careful reproduction and isolation.

expectedArtifacts: Regression test at the root-cause layer

**Reported 2026-10-01, with a screenshot.** In the plan graph, the sprint label in the left gutter (`SPRINT 1`, the goal, the ticket count) grows downward as a long goal wraps. It runs into the `CHECKPOINT 1 · HUMAN APPROVAL` divider pill, and the two texts are drawn over each other. In the screenshot, a five-line goal ("The card's words and pictures are ready: …") collides with the pill.

**Where:** the sprint node in `graph/nodes.tsx` (`.pg-sprint`, `.pg-sprint-goal`, `.pg-sprint-detail`), its placement in `graph/flowElements.ts` and `graph/graphModel.ts`, the divider styles in `graph/graph.css`.

**Fix:** the layout must never let the sprint label and the checkpoint divider (or a ticket card) overlap. Pick one approach and justify it in the submission:
- reserve vertical space for the label (size the sprint band to the label's height), or
- clamp the goal to a few lines with an ellipsis, with the full goal still available (for example a `title` or an expand control),
or a combination of both. The divider and its pill stay readable.

**TDD:** first write a failing layout test in `graphModel` or `flowElements` showing that, with a long goal (300 or more characters), the checkpoint divider sits below the label's bottom edge (or that the goal is clamped). Then fix it.

**Out of scope:** colors (the restyle tickets handle them); other graph layout changes.

tickets.body:
**Reported 2026-10-01.** When an epic completes, its overview (the final sprint report with the epic outcome, success-criteria results and notes) closes and can never be opened again. The record of what the epic achieved is lost from the UI.

**Likely cause:** `src/renderer/src/epic/workspaceLoad.ts` loads checkpoint data only for runs in `running` or `awaiting_checkpoint` (`CHECKPOINT_STATES`). `workspaceState.ts` closes the checkpoint view once `data.checkpoint` is `null` (`checkpointOpen: state.checkpointOpen && data.checkpoint !== null`). The outcome itself is stored: `.darkmechanicus/epics/<id>/state.json` has `outcome` (summary plus each criterion with `met` and `note`), and the run history keeps the sprint reports. Confirm this before fixing.

**Fix:**
- A completed epic shows a way to open its overview, for example an "Epic report" or "Overview" button in the run bar or header. It shows the outcome summary, every success criterion with met or not met and its note, and the sprint reports.
- The overview is read-only, with no approve, retry or follow-up actions.
- It stays open right after the final checkpoint is approved, instead of disappearing.
- It still works after restarting the app and after the repository is cloned elsewhere (it comes from the portable state).
- Use the completed "MCP connection test" epic in this repository as a real fixture to check against.

**TDD:** first write failing tests for the load and state logic for completed runs (`workspaceLoad`, `workspaceState`) and for the read-only rendering. Then fix.

**Out of scope:** the overview's text layout (the next ticket fixes the one-word-per-line text); restyling.

reasoning.rationale: Changes when checkpoint data loads and how the view behaves across run states, with tests for each.

expectedArtifacts: Load and state tests for completed runs
Screenshots of a completed epic overview

tickets.body:
**Reported 2026-10-01.** In the completed epic overview, some text is squeezed into a column about one word wide, so each word sits on its own line and the overview is unreadable. It could not be checked again because the overview disappears (the persistence ticket fixes that, so this ticket waits for it).

**Reproduce:** open the completed "MCP connection test" epic's overview at a few window widths (for example 1024, 1280 and 1440 px). Check the summary, the EPIC OUTCOME and EXIT CRITERIA lines with their notes, the ACCEPTED and FAILED rows, and the gate column.

**Suspects in `checkpoint/checkpoint.css`:**
- the two-column layout `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 1fr) 360px`;
- `.cp-row`, where an `auto` third column can starve the `minmax(0, 1fr)` text column;
- flex items with no `min-width` or `flex-basis`, which shrink to their narrowest content.

Find the real cause and fix it, without hard-coding widths for one screen size.

**Out of scope:** colors and the restyle; the persistence fix.

reasoning.rationale: A CSS layout bug, reproduced at fixed widths and checked with screenshots.
